text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.55% today to close at $150.80, its highest level in two weeks, as oil prices surged on escalating Middle East tensions. Brent crude topped $116 a barrel—a six-month high—after Saudi Arabia reported intercepting Iranian-backed Houthi missiles and drones, and amid reports of potential U.S. military action against Iran. For an integrated oil company like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices flow directly to the bottom line through increased revenue on barrels sold.

This move caps a remarkable two-week rally of 12.45%, driven by a consistent tightening of global oil supplies tied to regional conflict. The gap between world oil ($115.22) and U.S. oil ($107.89) has also widened, signaling growing concern about Middle East supply disruptions reaching international markets—a dynamic that favors large producers with diverse geographic exposure and the ability to benefit from premium global pricing.
